what: WorldForge v2 M0 L4 run 2 (PREFIX=m0_l4b) on the WorldForgeBaseline lab after the row 2b fixes (c646a4f5: door spurs anchor outside the found door, loud spur failures, plan hash = identity only) plus the uncommitted worldforge_status site_list field. Predictions were written before any result was read: m0_l4b_predictions.json.

results_vs_predictions.P1_plan_hash: CONFIRMED: 9693137997320541182 before and after the build (the F7 value; run 1 read 10638243061351388589).
results_vs_predictions.P2_town_spurs: NOT CONFIRMED - the count did not move: 'door spurs: 2 planned from 5 realized doors, 3 too steep' again. But the failures are now loud, and the numbers refute run 1's hypothesis: 'door (-10310,-9464 y1296) -> street (-10315,-9464 y1314): 6 cells, drop 18 micro, cap 2 micro/cell' (and the same for z -9401, -9374). The doorstep ground is 18 micro (2 cubes) BELOW the street edge 5 micro away - no straight ramp can do that in 6 cells; the spur start was never the cause for these three lots. The real defect is upstream: those lots' terrace pads are graded 2 cubes below the adjacent street surface (pad/street grade mismatch) - logged as a generator finding, not M0's.
results_vs_predictions.P3_site_outcomes: CHANGED, for the better: sites 3, 4 and 7 (hamlets) now BUILD (3, 3, 4 buildings; gates 10/10, 10/10, 14/14 walkable) - run 1 refused all three on a longhouse street->door pinch of 1 micro. Site 6's longhouse pinch is gone too (now 1 blocked of 17: the blacksmith @-1004,1404, still refused). The cluster path network and the spurs now meet the FOUND door's outside cell, which closes the 1-micro gap at the longhouse doors. Town (site 0): still refused on the hall_house @-1160,-1091 pinch (same cells as run 1 and the F7 class). Site 1: no plots (unchanged). Ledger: 5 built / 3 refused (run 1: 2 / 6; F7: 8 / 0 with two pinched sites shipped).
results_vs_predictions.P4_capture: NOT DONE - the script's capture step crashed: python on Windows cannot open the bash-style /c/... path ('FileNotFoundError'), so no target was chosen, no A/B, no screenshots. Fixed in the script (cygpath -m) for run 3.
results_vs_predictions.P6_duration: 282.5 s (prediction 290-320 s; 5 sites built this time, so cheaper than predicted per-site)

new_finding_from_the_loud_numbers: The three town lots whose spurs fail (general_store @-1146,-1058, bakery @-1145,-1044, hall_house @-1160,-1058) all PASSED the gate's 'street -> door' route. The probe settles (free-falls, no drop limit) after every step and checkRoutes asked only start -> goal, so a walker that falls off the 2-cube street edge onto the doorstep counts as 'walkable' although it can never climb back. This is a gate hole (a one-way cliff passes), pinned as row 2c: SettlementWalkabilityTest.AOneWayDropIsNotWalkable (red: walkable=1 on an 18-micro drop) -> checkRoutes requires the way back as well and reports one_way.
what_changed_the_hamlets: Not isolated to one cause by this run: row 2b changed both the spur/path anchor (outside the found door instead of the marker) and nothing else in the hamlet path. The longhouse pinches of run 1 were 1-micro gaps right at the door cell; a path that now ends at the door's outside cell paves that cell. A per-site A/B (same seed, marker anchor vs door anchor) would isolate it; not run.
caveats: the hash stability claim is one pristine-DB boot plus one build on one seed
